page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 63.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits top-tier single-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance in stress-ng, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10%. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores also place in this top tier. Conversely, multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and Passmark CPU and memory scores fall within the average range. For language model workloads, text generation with a small 135M model achieves top-tier speeds, whereas prompt processing with a medium 7B model is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and substantial memory-to-core ratio, the c4d-highmem-8 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The hardware configuration is suited for memory-bound applications, single-threaded data processing, text processing, database operations, and lightweight language model text generation.
